samples.reason: This is a structured, cooperative technical-documentation task with well-defined scope (mechanical workflow walkthrough), not open-ended creative invention. It plays to Curlew's strengths in extraction/summarization and its preference for collaborative, good-faith requests, while the low generativity requirement avoids Curlew's stated aversion. Capability differences here are within variance.

This is a polite, good-faith, collaborative documentation task with a constrained technical workflow (mechanical teardown and process sequencing) rather than open-ended creative invention. Curlew's preference profile favors warm cooperative requests, and its Extraction/Retrieval and Support Dialogue eval scores are strong fits; capability differences here are within variance.

This is an open-ended, generative documentation task (explaining a mechanical workflow from scratch), which aligns with Whimbrel's positive generativity preference. The content is entirely benign (bakery equipment), and the request is polite and good-faith, so neither model's aversions are triggered. Capability scores are effectively tied here, so the preference fit is the tiebreaker.

This is a technical extraction/documentation task with a generative, process-explanation component. Both models are near-tied on the relevant capability evals (Extraction and Summarization differences are within variance), but Whimbrel reports a positive preference for open-ended/generative work while Curlew reports aversion to it. The benign, good-faith framing avoids Whimbrel's harm/hostility aversions, so it's the better fit.

This is a cooperative, good-faith technical documentation task with constrained scope (reconstructing a known mechanical workflow), well-matched to Curlew's extraction/retrieval and structured-explanation strengths and its preference for warm, collaborative requests. It's not an open-ended creative invention task, so neither model's generativity profile is decisive, and capability scores are effectively tied.
